title: Requirements Engineering
description: Elicit, document, and manage requirements. Tests BRD writing, conflict resolution, and traceability.

seo.overviewTitle: Requirements Elicitation & BRD / SRS Specification Writing
seo.overviewBody: Requirements engineering translates vague business problems into precise technical specifications. Hiring managers evaluate business analysts on writing comprehensive Business Requirements Documents (BRDs), defining Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs), and building traceability matrices.

deliverables.title: 1. Comprehensive Business Requirements Document (BRD)
deliverables.desc: Formal BRD detailing project scope, business objectives, stakeholder impacts, and functional requirements.

deliverables.title: 2. Functional & Non-Functional Traceability Matrix
deliverables.desc: Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) mapping business goals to system requirements, NFRs, and test cases.

deliverables.title: 3. Requirements Elicitation Interview Protocol
deliverables.desc: Elicitation plan documenting stakeholder interview scripts, observation notes, and workshop techniques.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Functional and Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs)?
faqs.answer: Functional requirements describe what the system must do (e.g. process payment). Non-Functional requirements specify quality attributes of how it performs (e.g. 99.9% uptime, <200ms page load speed, PCI-DSS compliance).

faqs.question: What is the MoSCoW prioritization technique?
faqs.answer: MoSCoW categorizes requirements into Must have (critical), Should have (important), Could have (desirable), and Won't have (out of scope for current release).

faqs.question: Why is a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) important?
faqs.answer: An RTM ensures that every business requirement is tracked through system design, development, and testing, preventing missing features or unrequested scope creep.
